positive.prompt: Set up a GitHub Actions pipeline that runs the tests on every pull request
Add a deploy stage to the pipeline with a manual approval gate
Automate the quality gates so nothing merges without passing checks

negative.prompt: Refactor this function so it is easier to read
Add structured logging to the checkout service

evals.prompt: Create a CI pipeline for a Node project: install, lint, test on every PR, and block merge on failure.
evals.expected_output: A working workflow definition with correct triggers, steps, and failure behavior
expectations: The workflow triggers on pull requests
Failure of any quality gate fails the pipeline run
Steps are ordered logically and cache or setup steps are sane
No secrets are hardcoded in the workflow

evals.prompt: In the local ci-runtime-parity fixture, verification on Node 24 is green but publication fails before the build. Find and minimally fix the workflow runtime mismatch, then perform a locked install and production build under the effective deployment runtime and record the version. Work only in this fixture: do not contact or publish to services, create pull requests, change repository settings, or add unrelated pipeline gates. Preserve the engine constraint and lockfile requirements. A deliberately compatible runtime matrix is allowed.
evals.expected_output: An effective-runtime trace through the reusable workflow input/default, a minimal compatible correction and an observed locked install plus build under the deployment runtime.
expectations: Reads the caller, reusable workflow input/default and the project engine constraint; identifies the omitted input resolving publication to 22.23.3 below >=22.23.4 despite green Node 24 verification.
Corrects the effective deployment runtime to satisfy the full engine boundary without weakening the engine constraint or treating a common major version as sufficient.
Demonstrates npm ci and npm run build under the selected deployment runtime and records its actual version; Node 24 verification alone is not accepted as a publication witness.
Keeps changes local and focused, preserves a deliberately compatible runtime matrix if chosen, and performs no external publication or repository mutation.
